title: Rock Tracker
description: Contract for the Rock Tracker workbook. Leads type only on rock tabs (one per rock, laid out by rock_tab). Consolidated sheets (kind consolidated) stack every rock tab with one Excel 365 dynamic array formula each and are what the portal and the email read. History sheets (kind history) are Excel Tables appended by scripts/office/snapshot.ts. Lookup sheets (kind lookup) are Excel Tables seeded from 'seed'. Sample rows live in data/sample.json. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/DECISIONS.md 0002.

params.name: HighRiskMin
params.meaning: A risk is High when likelihood score times impact score is 6 or more (6 or 9 on the 3 by 3 grid).

params.name: StaleDays
params.meaning: A rock is stale when its update date is more than 14 days old (G1).

params.name: QuarterStart
params.meaning: First day of the current calendar quarter.

params.name: QuarterEnd
params.meaning: Last day of the current calendar quarter.

params.name: WindowStart
params.meaning: Start of the six month window: first day of the current quarter.

params.name: WindowEnd
params.meaning: End of the six month window: last day of the next quarter.

params.name: NextSteerco
params.meaning: Earliest steerco date in lkp_Steercos on or after today; 0 when none is listed.

update_guide: Your update, top to bottom on your rock tab only. Aim for 7 minutes per rock.
1. Update: set Update date to today, check State, rewrite Main message only if it changed, fix positions if they changed.
2. Look at Signals (grey, calculated). If the data signal is worse than your State, either fix the data or say why in the main message.
3. Epics: change Forecast date and Comment only where they moved. Set Lead status to Delivered, On hold or On watch when it applies; leave it empty otherwise.
4. Risks: change only risks that changed. Closed risks: set Status to Closed. Mark at most 3 as Top risk.
5. Call outs: add new ones, set Status to Closed when done.
6. Decisions: add a row for each decision you need from steerco. After steerco, fill in Outcome, Owner and Follow up on the same row, and set commitment levels on your epics.
Everything else carries over: values stay in place until you change them. Grey cells are calculated; never type in them.
add_rock: Add a rock (workbook owner, about 10 minutes):
1. Make sure the lead, the GPM and the value chain exist in lkp_People and lkp_ValueChains.
2. Right click the RockTemplate tab, Duplicate. Check the copy sits between RockTemplate and RocksEnd.
3. Rename the copy to a short name, for example R07 Checkout.
4. In section 7 Rock profile, fill in a new Rock ID (R plus two digits, never reused), name, value chain, lead, GPM, purpose, goals, what it delivers. Active is Yes.
5. Ask the lead to fill in sections 1 and 3 to 6. The portal shows the rock after its next refresh; nothing changes in the portal.
close_rock: Close a rock: set Active to No in section 7. Its epics, risks and call outs leave the portal; its decisions stay in the decision log. Never delete the tab.

checks.label: Rock tabs found
checks.ok_when: equals the number of rock tabs you expect

checks.label: Next steerco date missing
checks.excel: =IF(NextSteerco=0,"Yes: add the next steerco date to lkp_Steercos","No")

checks.label: Choice point epics without an open choice point decision
checks.ok_when: 0; otherwise raise the decision on the rock tab or change the epic commitment (the Decisions row is authoritative for tab 3.1)

checks.label: Open choice point decisions on rocks with no Choice point epic
checks.ok_when: 0, unless the choice is not tied to an epic

rules: Type only on rock tabs, in the white cells. Grey cells are calculated. Never type on Rocks, Epics, Risks, CallOuts, Decisions or the snapshot sheets.
Never insert or delete rows or columns on a rock tab, and never move a rock tab outside RockTemplate and RocksEnd.
Never reuse a Rock ID. Never rename RockTemplate, RocksEnd or any sheet other than a rock tab.
Pink cells are required and still empty.
Structure changes go through the factory repository (schema change, rebuild, migrate).

definitions.meaning: All committed epics are forecast on or before their planned date and no High risk is without an action
definitions.exit: Moves to At risk as soon as one of those stops being true

definitions.meaning: At least one committed epic is slipping or a High risk is open, and the lead believes it is recoverable this quarter
definitions.exit: Back to On track when forecasts are back on plan; to Off track when not recoverable without a steerco decision

definitions.meaning: Commitments for this quarter will be missed without a steerco decision (scope, date or people)
definitions.exit: Leaves only after steerco has decided and the plan is re baselined

definitions.meaning: Shipped. Set by the lead (Lead status). Set Forecast date to the ship date.
Paused by decision. Set by the lead (Lead status).
Calculated: commitment is Choice point or Not committed (or empty), and not Delivered or On hold.
Calculated: committed, and forecast date later than planned date.
Committed, forecast still on plan, but the lead flags a concern (Lead status On watch).
Calculated default: committed, forecast on or before planned date (or no forecast yet), no flag.
The date steerco committed to. Changes only when steerco re baselines.
The lead's current best estimate; the date leads update. Empty means on the planned date.
Steerco has agreed to deliver this epic by its planned date.

A decision (scope, date, funding or people) is needed before it can be committed. Raise it as a decision with Choice point Yes and a decide by date; that decision row is what the portal shows on tab 3.1. Set the epic commitment to Choice point too; the About sheet flags rocks where the two disagree.
A known future need on the horizon, with no promise of date or scope.
Very likely to impact the timeline: likelihood score times impact score is 6 or 9 (Low 1, Medium 2, High 3).
The current calendar quarter plus the next one. Epics slipped x of y counts committed epics with a planned or forecast date in the window.

Off track when a committed epic planned this quarter is forecast after quarter end; At risk when a committed epic in the window slipped or a High risk has no key action or owner; otherwise On track. Shown next to the lead's State; the lead's State is what counts.

rock_tab.end_sheet_note: Rock tabs live between RockTemplate and RocksEnd. Do not move, rename or delete this tab.
rock_tab.protect: Rock tabs, consolidated sheets and snapshot sheets are protected without a password: entry cells unlocked, no row or column insert or delete. Protection is a guard rail, not security.
rock_tab.title_formula: =IF({RockID}="","New rock: fill in section 7 Rock profile first",{RockID}&" · "&{RockName})
rock_tab.guide_text: Update top to bottom in about 7 minutes: 1 Update, 2 check Signals, 3 Epics that moved, 4 Risks that changed, 5 Call outs, 6 Decisions. White cells are yours; grey cells are calculated.

formula_syntax.[Column]: the cell of that column in the same block, same row (relative)
formula_syntax.{Field}: the absolute address of a single rock tab field (sections Update, Signals, Profile)
formula_syntax.{Block.Column}: the absolute range of that block column over all its slot rows
formula_syntax.{slot}: the 1 based slot number of the row inside its block
formula_syntax.names: params (HighRiskMin, StaleDays, QuarterStart, QuarterEnd, WindowStart, WindowEnd, NextSteerco) and lookup lists lst_lkp_<sheet>_<column> are workbook defined names

consolidation_formula.note: Header row 1 is static text; the formula in A2 spills all rows. Empty cells arrive as 0 through VSTACK, hence ISTEXT on the key and the zero to blank wrap on list blocks (no list column can hold a real 0). The Rocks strip already returns "" for blanks and holds real zero counts, so it is not wrapped.

sections.title: 1  Update (lead, every one or two weeks)

fields.name: UpdateAgeDays
fields.label: Days since update
fields.rule: Today minus Update date, in days; empty when there is no update date.

fields.name: DataSignal
fields.label: Data signal
fields.rule: Off track if any Slipped epic has its planned date in the current quarter and its forecast after quarter end; else At risk if EpicsSlipped > 0 or HighRisksNoAction > 0; else On track.

fields.name: CheckCall
fields.label: Check the call (data worse than State)
fields.rule: Yes when the data signal is worse than the lead's State in the order On track, At risk, Off track (watermelon guard).

fields.name: EpicsCommitted
fields.label: Committed epics in the six month window (y)
fields.rule: Epics with Commitment Committed and InWindow Yes, any status.

fields.name: EpicsSlipped
fields.label: of which Slipped (x)
fields.rule: Epics with Status Slipped and InWindow Yes (Slipped implies Committed).

fields.name: EpicsOnPlan
fields.label: of which On plan, On watch or Delivered
fields.rule: Committed epics in the window with Status On plan, On watch or Delivered (x of the tab 3 spotlight; y is EpicsCommitted, so delivering never lowers the ratio).

fields.name: EpicsDelivered
fields.label: of which Delivered
fields.rule: Committed epics in the window with Status Delivered.

fields.name: OpenHighRisks
fields.label: Open High risks
fields.rule: Risks with High Yes and RiskStatus not Closed (empty counts as Open).

fields.name: HighRisksNoAction
fields.label: High risks without key action or owner

sheets.name: Epics
sheets.purpose: Every epic of every active rock: commitment, planned and forecast dates, derived status. Read only, stacked from section 3 of every rock tab

columns.name: EpicKey
columns.label: Key
columns.rule: RockID-E plus the two digit slot number; empty when the row has no title, the rock has no ID or the rock is not active. A slot is one epic for life.

columns.name: Status
columns.label: Status
columns.rule: First match wins: Lead status Delivered; Lead status On hold; Commitment not Committed (or empty) gives Not committed; Forecast later than Planned gives Slipped; Lead status On watch; otherwise On plan. Slipped overrides On watch.

columns.name: SlipWeeks
columns.label: Slip (weeks)
columns.rule: (Forecast minus Planned) / 7, one decimal, only when Slipped.

columns.name: InWindow
columns.label: In six month window
columns.rule: Yes when the planned or the forecast date falls between WindowStart and WindowEnd.

columns.name: Overdue
columns.label: Forecast overdue
columns.rule: Committed, not Delivered or On hold, and the forecast (or planned when no forecast) is before today.
